_meta.source: NOAA CPC (ONI, RONI, weekly Niño 3.4); BoM Australia (relative Niño 3.4, Troup SOI)
_meta.notes: Five indices, each parsed from a machine-readable feed. No single spread is given across all five: they differ in region, baseline and averaging window, so a min/max across them would mix all three. Only pairs that differ in one variable are compared, and each is listed. A source that fails is omitted, never back-filled.

indices.label: ONI
indices.note: The index the harvest fit uses. Absolute anomaly against base periods CPC re-centres every five years.

indices.label: RONI
indices.note: CPC's strength index: Niño 3.4 minus the tropical-mean (20°N–20°S) anomaly for the same months, rescaled to ONI's variability. It removes long-term warming and also the tropics' own delayed response to El Niño, so the ONI–RONI gap shifts through an event.

indices.label: Weekly Niño 3.4
indices.note: One week, from a different SST analysis (OISST) on a fixed base. It is not a weekly version of ONI.

indices.label: Relative Niño 3.4
indices.note: BoM's operational ocean index since Sept 2025. Its threshold is +0.8, higher than CPC's +0.5.

indices.label: Troup SOI
indices.note: Air pressure between Tahiti and Darwin, not sea temperature. Negative is El Niño-like. A negative reading means the atmosphere is responding to the ocean, so the signal is coupled rather than SST-only.

iod.label: Indian Ocean Dipole (DMI)
iod.note: BoM treats ±0.4 °C sustained for about eight weeks as an IOD event; one week above is not an event yet.

comparisons.free_variable: baseline: ERSST v6, centred 30-year base periods vs relative to the tropical mean
comparisons.reading: Same agency, region and window. The gap comes from RONI's baseline: it subtracts the tropical mean and rescales, which removes long-term warming and this event's own warming of the tropics.

invalid_comparisons.why: 2 variables are free at once (baseline: ERSST v6, centred 30-year base periods vs OISST v2.1, fixed 1991–2020; window: JAS 2026, 3-month mean vs week centred on 30 Sep 2026 (27–3 Oct)). The gap mixes these differences, so no single cause can be read from it.

3 variables are free at once (agency: NOAA CPC vs BoM Australia; baseline: OISST v2.1, fixed 1991–2020 vs relative to the tropical mean; window: week centred on 30 Sep 2026 (27–3 Oct) vs week 28 Sep 2026 – 4 Oct 2026). The gap mixes these differences, so no single cause can be read from it.
